headline_marked: Towhid Hridoy slams [[historic double ton]] to lead Bangladesh fightback
headline: Towhid Hridoy slams historic double ton to lead Bangladesh fightback
summary: The young batter smashed an unbeaten 208, breaking multiple records and guiding Bangladesh to within touching distance of West Indies' first-innings total.
details: Towhid Hridoy rewrote the record books on day three of the second Test against West Indies in Sylhet, smashing his maiden Test double-century to lead a remarkable Bangladesh fightback. The middle-order batter remained unbeaten on 208 off 314 balls, with 19 fours and eight sixes, as Bangladesh reached 340-8, trailing by just 16 runs.

Hridoy surpassed Mominul Haque's record for the highest score in a maiden Test century by a Bangladeshi, going past the 181 Mominul scored against New Zealand in 2013. He also became the fourth Bangladeshi to score a Test double-century, joining the elite company of Mushfiqur Rahim, Shakib Al Hasan, and Tamim Iqbal.

The young batsman's explosive innings included a record-breaking eight sixes, surpassing Tamim Iqbal's previous mark of seven sixes in a Test innings. Hridoy also registered the highest individual Test score at the Sylhet International Cricket Stadium, eclipsing Mahmudul Hasan Joy's 171.

Furthermore, Hridoy shared a crucial 117-run eighth-wicket partnership with Taijul Islam (22), setting a new record for the venue. This partnership was vital in Bangladesh's recovery from a precarious 184-7, bringing the team back into contention in the match.

The records come as a significant turnaround for Hridoy, who had faced criticism for his previous dismissals. He might not have even played in this Test had Mominul Haque been fit, highlighting his determination and performance under pressure.

headline: 7 Bangladeshi nationals killed in Saudi road accident
summary: The victims, including a child, were traveling from Medina to Jeddah when a truck hit their bus from behind.
details: Seven Bangladeshi nationals, including a child, were killed in a road accident in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, on Saturday.
Fifteen other Bangladeshis were injured in the crash and have been admitted to a local hospital for treatment.
The accident occurred early Saturday morning while the victims were traveling from Medina to Jeddah.
According to local sources, a truck struck the bus carrying the Bangladeshi nationals from behind.
The deceased are members of several Bangladeshi families, including a child.
The Consul General of Bangladesh in Jeddah confirmed the incident to Prothom Alo on Saturday afternoon.
The Bangladesh Consulate has formally requested detailed information from local authorities regarding the casualties in Jizan, in the southwestern region of Saudi Arabia.
The bodies of the deceased have been kept in a local hospital morgue.
